Evidence & scope

Scoped methods, data-collection or experiment claims were read from the exact pinned preprint version by separate author, source-verifier and adversarial AI invocations. The full cited contexts, including conditions and model/table identities, are bound to approved observations; actual partial/full/unread scopes are retained in review records. This is not a complete-paper, latest-version, corpus, proof, labor, supplier-performance or experiment-reproduction audit. Work and version remain distinct and contribute at most one reviewed paper work.

Approved findings

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Quality Assured: Rethinking Annotation Strategies in Imaging AI (2407.17596v2) · paper method: Three instruction conditions contain 168 words/seven slides, 446 words/ten slides and 961 words/16 slides with pictures. Company workflows expose the same instructions to annotators and QA workers, and researchers compare outputs before/after QA using Dice, normalized surface distance and severe-error counts.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Quality Assured: Rethinking Annotation Strategies in Imaging AI (2407.17596v2) · paper method: With extended text or text-plus-picture instructions, two of four companies show no change in median Dice after QA and the other two show relative improvements below 2%; the main figure describes larger gains from better instructions than added QA in these surgical segmentation experiments.

cohort9.claim.qualityassured.qa-result

  • This is a within-project, instruction-dependent comparison, not a universal QA effect or a named supplier ranking; figure pixels were not separately inspected.

Approved evidence · As of 10 Nov 2026

Quality Assured: Rethinking Annotation Strategies in Imaging AI (2407.17596v2) · paper method: The surgical-instrument segmentation study obtains 57,648 instance masks on 4,050 unique laparoscopic frames using 216 annotators and 34 QA workers from four unnamed annotation companies plus 708 MTurk workers; these are repeated annotation units, not 57,648 unique images.
